column1: H5-D1FR-6.1;FR-6.2;FR-6.3P_H5Trajectory consistencyVehicle motion consistent with intended trajectoryVehicle motion inconsistent with intended trajectoryPASSCollapsing these situations removes information required to determine whether the vehicle follows the intended trajectory.Candidate

H5-D2SG-5;H-5;SR-5.3.2P_H5Road-boundary relationVehicle motion remains within road boundariesVehicle motion leaves road boundariesPASSCollapsing these situations removes information directly required to evaluate unintended leaving of the road.Candidate

H5-D3FR-6.6;FR-6.8;SR-5.4.1P_H5Speed-profile conditionSpeed condition compatible with road containmentSpeed condition threatens road containmentPASSThe speed condition is concern-relevant when it affects road containment, but it may impose the same preservation obligation as the road-boundary distinction.Candidate-Merge

H5-D4FR-6.10P_H5Vehicle positionVehicle position consistent with intended trajectory/road relationVehicle position inconsistent with intended trajectory/road relationPASSActual position supports trajectory and boundary evaluation; localization correctness itself is not treated as a phenomenon-level distinction.Candidate-Merge

H5-D5FR-6.5P_H5Steering effectSteering effect maintains intended trajectorySteering effect deviates from intended trajectoryPASSThe concern-relevant effect is vehicle motion relative to trajectory rather than correctness of the steering computation itself.Candidate-Merge

H5-D6FR-6.4.1P_H5Longitudinal-control update timingLongitudinal control values provided every 15 msLongitudinal control values not provided every 15 msFAILThe timed property concerns the control mechanism rather than a distinction between states of the declared Phenomenon of Interest.Reject-as-CRD

H5-D7FR-6.4.2;SR-5.3.1P_H5Lateral/steering-control timingLateral control values provided every 5 ms / steering commands timelyLateral control values not provided every 5 ms / steering commands lateFAILThe timed property concerns the control mechanism rather than trajectory-relative operational motion; it may instead establish a dependency or preservation condition.Reject-as-CRD
